statement: The parabola has equation $y^{2}=4ax$. (i) By implicit differentiation find $\\frac{dy}{dx}$ at the point $(at^{2},2at)$. (ii) Hence show that the tangent at this point is $ty=x+at^{2}$. (iii) Find where this tangent meets the $x$-axis.
solution: (i) $2y\\,dy/dx=4a$ so $dy/dx=2a/y$; at $(at^{2},2at)$ this is $1/t$. (ii) Tangent: $y-2at=(1/t)(x-at^{2})$, i.e. $ty-2at^{2}=x-at^{2}$, so $ty=x+at^{2}$. (iii) Set $y=0$: $0=x+at^{2}$, so it meets the $x$-axis at $x=-at^{2}$.
hints: Substitute the point into the point-slope form.
